as_told.title: Matthew Brown and the Immaculate Constellation document on transmedium UFOs

plain: A former Defense Department official named Matthew Brown is said to have found the secret Immaculate Constellation briefing because it had been wrongly uploaded to a shared government intelligence network called Intelink. Jeremy Corbell tells it this way, passing on what Brown told him, and Michels, crediting Corbell and the journalist George Knapp, says the document talks about "transmedium objects, UFOs going in and out of the water." The unsigned report on the program, which Brown later said he wrote, does speak of tracking "anomalous transmedium platforms", but it says only that its author got the material "while pursuing their lawful duties" at the Defense Department; the shared server and the misplaced upload are Corbell's account.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report says of how its author came to the material only that they "obtained access to this information while pursuing their lawful duties as an employee of the Department of Defense", and it speaks of the capacity "to detect, track, identify, and engage anomalous transmedium platforms". The transmedium objects Jesse Michels mentions are in it; the shared Intelink server and the misplaced upload are Jeremy Corbell's account.
